title: Potential Difference, Potential Due to a Point Charge, Potential Energy and Electron Volt
notes: **Potential difference:** work done per unit charge to move a test charge between two points: $\Delta V = W/q$.
**Potential due to point charge:** $V = kQ/r$. It is a scalar, so contributions from multiple charges add algebraically.
**Potential energy of two charges:** $U = kq_1q_2/r$. Positive $U$ means repulsive configuration; negative $U$ means attractive configuration.
**Relation between field and potential:** $E = -dV/dr$. The electric field is the negative gradient of the potential.
**Electron volt (eV):** the kinetic energy gained by an electron when accelerated through 1 V potential difference. $1\,\text{eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{J}$.
